newsitem.title: GERMANY: German mobile phone prices are Europe's highest.
newsitem.headline: German mobile phone prices are Europe's highest.

text.p: German mobile phone operators have the highest prices and among the lowest rates of usage in Europe, an industry association said on Monday, threatening to file a complaint with telecommunications regulators.

Based on a comparison of 60 minutes of calls made during peak hours and 30 minutes during off-peak periods, Mannesmann Mobilfunk's D2 digital cellular network was the most expensive provider in Europe, the Association of Private Telecommunications Service Providers (VAT) said.
Deutsche Telekom's D1 network ran a close second, followed by operators in Belgium, Switzerland, Germany's E-Plus network, France, Austria, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Britain and Denmark.
With 70.8 mobile phone users per 1,000 residents, Germany was ranked 12th in Europe.
The VAT said the main reason for the high prices and low usage rates was "the lack of interest of the two largest network operators in entering real price competition."

"The mutual behaviour of the two D networks in price policies ... has led to the replacement of the one-time monopoly with oligopolistic structures," said VAT chairman Gerd Eickers. "There is no real price competition."
The VAT statement added that one way to correct the situation would be for mobile phone operators to offer customers a discount on large volumes of calling time.
"The VAT will satisfy the justified claim of its members if necessary through a legal complaint," it said.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097 150 at a discount for large volume blocks of calling time
